title: No eating on the metro
goal: Ride the Dubai Metro with Sēf and learn the rules: where you can sit and what's not allowed
tip: A passive participle on the pattern maCCūC says what has been done to something: katab 'wrote' → maktūb 'written', manaʿ 'banned' → mamnūʿ 'banned'. For a rule, put a verbal noun after it: mamnūʿ il-akil 'no eating'. masmūḥ is the opposite: it-taṣwīr masmūḥ 'photos are allowed'.
grammar: passive participle maCCūC: mamnūʿ, maktūb, masmūḥ
dialogue: B
يلا نقعد هني، الكراسي فاضية
yalla nigʿid hni, il-karāsi fāẓya
Come on, let's sit here, the seats are free.
A
لا، هذا حق الحريم والعيال. شوف، مكتوب على الباب
la, hādha ḥagg il-ḥarīm w il-ʿyāl. shūf, maktūb ʿala l-bāb
No, this part's for women and children. Look, it says so on the door.
B
آسف، ما شفته! عيل وين نقعد؟
āsif, ma shiftah! ʿayal wēn nigʿid?
Sorry, I didn't see it! Where do we sit, then?
A
هناك. وترا ممنوع الأكل والشرب في المترو
hnāk. w tara mamnūʿ il-akil w ish-shurb fi l-mitrō
Over there. And by the way, no eating or drinking on the metro.
B
صج؟ ولا حتى الماي؟
ṣij? wala ḥatta l-māy?
Really? Not even water?
A
ولا حتى الماي. ممنوع، وفي غرامة
wala ḥatta l-māy. mamnūʿ, w fī gharāma
Not even water. It's not allowed, and there's a fine.
B
زين، بتريا لين ننزل. والتصوير مسموح؟
zēn, batrayya lēn ninzil. w it-taṣwīr masmūḥ?
OK, I'll wait till we get off. And are photos allowed?
A
مسموح، بس لا تصور الناس
masmūḥ, bas la tṣawwir in-nās
They're allowed, but don't take photos of people.
items: with a feminine noun: mamnūʿa (ممنوعة); the opposite: masmūḥ (مسموح)
mamnūʿ + an activity is how rules and signs are said: mamnūʿ it-tadkhīn = no smoking
maktūb = written; maktūb hni = it says here
il-ḥarīm = women; for men: ḥagg ir-ryāyīl (حق الرياييل)
a fine: gharāma; a traffic ticket: mukhālafa (مخالفة)
don't take photos of people (to a man)
to a woman: la tṣawwrīn in-nās (لا تصورين الناس)
I'll wait till we get off
plural things take the feminine: fāẓya; one seat: il-kursi fāẓi
culture: The Dubai Metro has a section for women and children, clearly marked on the platform and the doors: men don't sit there. Eating and drinking aren't allowed on the trains, and you can be fined. Taking photos of people without asking can break UAE privacy law, so ask first or keep strangers out of the picture.

title: The lift's out of order
goal: Plan a meeting with Maryam at the office when the lift is broken, the room is booked and the manager's line is busy
tip: Participles describe a state: ḥajaz 'booked' → maḥjūz 'booked, taken'; mashghūl 'busy'. Form II verbs (doubled middle letter) make theirs with m-: sakkar 'shut' → msakkar 'shut'; mʿaṭṭal 'out of order' has the same shape. With a feminine noun add -a: il-ghurfa maḥjūza.
grammar: participles for states: maḥjūz, mashghūl; Form II with m-: mʿaṭṭal, msakkar
dialogue: B
صباح الخير يا مريم. اللفت معطل، طلعت على ريولي!
ṣabāḥ il-khēr yā Maryam. il-lift mʿaṭṭal, ṭilaʿt ʿala ryūli!
Morning, Maryam. The lift's out of order, I walked up!
A
صباح النور. هيه، معطل من أمس
ṣabāḥ in-nūr. hē, mʿaṭṭal min ams
Morning. Yes, it's been out of order since yesterday.
B
عندنا اجتماع الساعة عشر. غرفة الاجتماعات فاضية؟
ʿindana ijtimāʿ is-sāʿa ʿashr. ghurfat il-ijtimāʿāt fāẓya?
We've got a meeting at ten. Is the meeting room free?
A
لا، محجوزة لين الظهر
la, maḥjūza lēn iẓ-ẓuhur
No, it's booked till midday.
B
عيل نسويه في مكتبج؟
ʿayal nsawwīh fi maktabich?
Shall we have it in your office, then?
A
زين. بس المدير لازم يدري. اتصلت فيه، وتلفونه مشغول
zēn. bas il-mudīr lāzim yadri. ittaṣalt fīh, w tilifōnah mashghūl
OK. But the manager needs to know. I called him, and his line's busy.
B
بطرش له رسالة. وانتي، تبين قهوة؟
baṭarrish-lah risāla. w inti, tabīn gahwa?
I'll send him a message. And would you like a coffee?
A
ودي، بس الكافتيريا مسكرة اليوم!
widdi, bas il-kāftērya msakkara l-yōm!
I'd love one, but the cafeteria's closed today!
items: out of order, not working (a lift, a machine)
with a feminine noun: mʿaṭṭala (معطلة); also: kharbān (خربان)
min yōmēn = for two days now
with a feminine noun: maḥjūza (محجوزة); hādha l-kursi maḥjūz? = is this seat taken?
to a man: fi maktabak (في مكتبك)
his line's busy, his phone's engaged
he has to know, he needs to be told
she has to know: lāzim tadri
to her: baṭarrish-lha risāla (بطرش لها رسالة)

title: I'm not used to this heat
goal: On a hot afternoon, tell Sēf what you're used to and what you aren't
tip: Form V verbs (tʿawwad 'got used to') make their participle with mit-: mitʿawwid 'used to'. It works like an adjective: ana mitʿawwid ʿala l-ḥarr 'I'm used to the heat' (a woman: mitʿawwda). A verb can follow straight after: mitʿawwid anām mitʼakhkhir 'I'm used to going to bed late'.
grammar: Form V participle with mit-: mitʿawwid 'used to'
dialogue: A
شفيك؟ ويهك أحمر!
shfīk? wiyhak aḥmar!
What's wrong? Your face is red!
B
حر وايد! أنا مب متعود على هالحر
ḥarr wāyid! ana mub mitʿawwid ʿala hal-ḥarr
It's so hot! I'm not used to this heat.
A
عادي، بتتعود. أنا متعود عليه من صغري
ʿādi, bititʿawwad. ana mitʿawwid ʿalēh min ṣighri
Don't worry, you'll get used to it. I've been used to it since I was little.
B
في لندن ما نشوف الشمس وايد!
fi Landan ma nshūf ish-shams wāyid!
In London we don't see the sun much!
A
عيل انت متعود على البرد
ʿayal inta mitʿawwid ʿala l-bard
So you're used to the cold.
B
هيه. وهني الناس متعودين يطلعون بالليل، صح؟
hē. w hni n-nās mitʿawwdīn yiṭlaʿūn bil-lēl, ṣaḥḥ?
Yes. And here people are used to going out at night, right?
A
صح، في الصيف كل شي بالليل
ṣaḥḥ, fi ṣ-ṣēf kill shay bil-lēl
Right, in summer everything happens at night.
B
زين، أنا متعود أنام متأخر!
zēn, ana mitʿawwid anām mitʼakhkhir!
Good, I'm used to going to bed late!
items: a woman: mub mitʿawwda (مب متعودة); Kuwait: mū mitʿawwid (مو متعود)
niḥin mitʿawwdīn = we're used to it
since he was little: min ṣighrah (من صغره)
your face is red (to a man)
to a woman: wiyhich aḥmar (ويهج أحمر)
culture: In the hottest months much of daily life in the UAE moves to the evening. People run errands early in the morning or after maghrib, malls and cafés stay busy late, and parks and beaches fill up at night once it cools a little. Midday is for staying indoors.

title: Driving lessons
goal: Tell Sēf how your driving lessons are going and when your test is
tip: A verbal noun names an activity: sāg 'drove' → is-swāga 'driving', diras 'studied' → id-dirāsa 'studying', zār 'visited' → iz-zyāra 'the visit'. Use it like any noun: is-swāga hni ṣaʿba 'driving here is hard', imtiḥān is-swāga 'the driving test'. Learn each one with its verb.
dialogue: A
شو أخبار السواقة؟
shu akhbār is-swāga?
How's the driving going?
B
صعبة وايد! هني الكل يسوق بسرعة
ṣaʿba wāyid! hni l-kill ysūg b-surʿa
Really hard! Everyone here drives fast.
A
صج. وفي لندن ما كنت تسوق؟
ṣij. w fi Landan ma kint tsūg?
True. And didn't you drive in London?
B
لا، كنت أروح بالباص وبالمترو
la, kint arūḥ bil-bāṣ w bil-mitrō
No, I used to take the bus and the tube.
A
زين. ومتى امتحان السواقة؟
zēn. w mita imtiḥān is-swāga?
Right. And when's the driving test?
B
الأسبوع الياي إن شاء الله. خايف شوي
il-usbūʿ il-yāy in shāʼ allāh. khāyif shwayy
Next week, God willing. I'm a bit nervous.
A
لا تخاف. أول ما تاخذ الرخصة، نسوق في البر!
la tkhāf. awwal ma tākhidh ir-rukhṣa, nsūg fi l-barr!
Don't worry. As soon as you get your licence, we'll go driving in the desert!
B
البر؟ لا لا، السواقة في البر بعدين!
il-barr? la la, is-swāga fi l-barr baʿdēn!
The desert? No, no, desert driving can wait!
items: sāg = he drove; the driver: is-sāyig (السايق)
shu akhbār id-dirāsa? = how are your studies going?
I drive: asūg (أسوق); she drives: tsūg (تسوق)
a masculine thing: ṣaʿb wāyid (صعب وايد)
tākhidh ir-rukhṣa = you get your licence
didn't you (use to) drive? (to a man)
to a woman: ma kinti tsūgīn? (ما كنتي تسوقين؟)
we drive in the desert, we go desert driving

title: What do you do in your free time?
goal: Ask a group of Sēf's friends about their hobbies and say what you like doing
tip: For hobbies, put a verbal noun after aḥibb 'I like' or hiwāyti 'my hobby is': aḥibb is-sibāḥa 'I like swimming', hiwāyti ṣ-ṣēd 'my hobby's fishing'. A verb works too, with nothing in between: aḥibb asbaḥ 'I like to swim'. To a group: shu tḥibbūn? 'what do you like?'
grammar: verbal nouns after aḥibb and hiwāyti: is-sibāḥa, iṣ-ṣēd, il-giraya
dialogue: B
يا شباب، شو تسوون في وقت الفراغ؟
yā shabāb, shu tsawwūn fi wagt il-farāgh?
Guys, what do you do in your free time?
A
كلنا نلعب كورة. وأنا هوايتي الصيد
killna nilʿab kūra. w ana hiwāyti ṣ-ṣēd
We all play football. And my hobby's fishing.
B
الصيد؟ حلو! وين تصيد؟
iṣ-ṣēd? ḥilu! wēn tṣīd?
Fishing? Nice! Where do you fish?
A
في البحر، بالطراد. وانت، شو تحب؟
fi l-baḥar, biṭ-ṭarrād. w inta, shu tḥibb?
At sea, from a boat. And you, what do you like?
B
أحب القراية والسباحة. انتو تحبون السباحة؟
aḥibb il-giraya w is-sibāḥa. intu tḥibbūn is-sibāḥa?
I like reading and swimming. Do you guys like swimming?
A
هيه، كل جمعة نروح البحر. تعال ويانا!
hē, kill jumʿa nrūḥ il-baḥar. taʿāl wiyyāna!
Yes, we go to the beach every Friday. Come with us!
B
أكيد! بس الصيد ما جربته. علموني!
akīd! bas iṣ-ṣēd ma jarrabtah. ʿallmūni!
Definitely! But I've never tried fishing. You'll have to teach me!
A
أبشر! بتستانس، بس لازم تصحى بدري
abshir! bitistānis, bas lāzim tiṣḥa badri
You're on! You'll love it, but you'll have to get up early.
items: fi wagt il-farāgh = in your free time
a hobby: hiwāya (هواية); your hobby: hiwāytak (to a man), hiwāytich (to a woman)
to one man: tḥibb; to one woman: tḥibbīn (تحبين)
a feminine thing: ma jarrabt-ha (ما جربتها)
to one man: ʿallimni (علمني); to one woman: ʿallmīni (علميني)

title: It was supposed to be Thursday
goal: At the office, sort out a changed deadline with Maryam: what you're supposed to do and what should have happened
tip: il-mafrūẓ + a present verb says what's expected: il-mafrūẓ nṭarrish il-ʿarẓ il-yōm 'we're supposed to send the presentation today'. It never changes. Put kān in front for what should have happened: kān il-mafrūẓ ygūlūn-li 'they should have told me'.
grammar: il-mafrūẓ + verb 'supposed to'; kān il-mafrūẓ 'should have'
dialogue: A
ترا المفروض نطرش العرض للمدير اليوم
tara l-mafrūẓ nṭarrish il-ʿarẓ lil-mudīr il-yōm
Just so you know, we're supposed to send the presentation to the manager today.
B
اليوم؟ المفروض يوم الخميس!
il-yōm? il-mafrūẓ yōm il-khamīs!
Today? It was supposed to be Thursday!
A
لا، غيروا الموعد. ما قالوا لك؟
la, ghayyaraw il-mawʿid. ma gālaw-lak?
No, they moved the deadline. Didn't they tell you?
B
لا والله! كان المفروض يقولون لي
la wallāh! kān il-mafrūẓ ygūlūn-li
No, they didn't! They should have told me.
A
ما عليه. المدير يبيه قبل الساعة أربع
ma ʿalēh. il-mudīr yabīh gabil is-sāʿa arbaʿ
Never mind. The manager wants it before four.
B
زين. المفروض أسوي الأرقام، صح؟
zēn. il-mafrūẓ asawwi l-argām, ṣaḥḥ?
OK. I'm supposed to do the figures, right?
A
هيه، وأنا أكتب الإيميل حق المدير
hē, w ana aktib il-īmēl ḥagg il-mudīr
Yes, and I'll write the email to the manager.
B
ماشي. طرشي لي الملف الحين
māshi. ṭarrshī-li l-malaff il-ḥīn
OK. Send me the file now.
items: it never changes: il-mafrūẓ trūḥ = you're supposed to go; il-mafrūẓ arūḥ = I'm supposed to go
kān il-mafrūẓ trūḥ = you should have gone
I'm supposed to do, I should do
they changed the date, they moved the deadline
il-mawʿid = the appointment, the agreed time
didn't they tell you? (to a man)
to a woman: ma gālaw-lich? (ما قالوا لج؟)

title: You don't have to bring anything
goal: Sēf passes on his uncle's dinner invitation: find out what you don't have to do and what you mustn't do
tip: mub lāzim + verb usually means 'you don't have to': mub lāzim tyīb shay 'no need to bring anything'. To forbid something, put ma after lāzim: lāzim ma titʼakhkhar 'you mustn't be late'. mub lāzim can also mean 'better not', so lāzim ma is the clear way to say 'mustn't'.
grammar: mub lāzim 'don't have to' vs lāzim ma 'mustn't'
dialogue: A
عمي بو راشد عازمنا على العشا يوم الخميس
ʿammi Bū Rāshid ʿāzimna ʿala l-ʿasha yōm il-khamīs
My uncle Bū Rāshid has invited us to dinner on Thursday.
B
حلو! لازم أييب شي وياي؟
ḥilu! lāzim ayīb shay wiyyāy?
Great! Do I need to bring anything?
A
لا، مب لازم تييب شي. بس تعال
la, mub lāzim tyīb shay. bas taʿāl
No, you don't have to bring anything. Just come.
B
وشو ألبس؟ لازم كندورة؟
w shu albas? lāzim kandūra?
And what do I wear? Do I have to wear a kandura?
A
مب لازم. البس شي محترم وبس
mub lāzim. ilbas shay miḥtaram w bas
No need. Just wear something smart.
B
زين. وفي شي لازم ما أسويه؟
zēn. w fī shay lāzim ma asawwīh?
OK. And is there anything I mustn't do?
A
لازم ما تتأخر. عمي ما يحب التأخير
lāzim ma titʼakhkhar. ʿammi ma yḥibb it-taʼkhīr
You mustn't be late. My uncle doesn't like people being late.
B
لا تخاف، بكون هناك قبلك!
la tkhāf, bakūn hnāk gablak!
Don't worry, I'll be there before you!
items: you don't have to bring anything (to a man)
to a woman: mub lāzim tyībīn shay (مب لازم تييبين شي)
lāzim ma ninsa = we mustn't forget
you mustn't be late (to a man)
to a woman: lāzim ma titʼakhkharīn (لازم ما تتأخرين)
to a woman: ilbasi shay miḥtaram (البسي شي محترم)
with a feminine noun: miḥtarama (محترمة); rayyāl miḥtaram = a decent man
culture: Guests aren't expected to bring anything to a majlis dinner, but turning up on time and dressed neatly matters. A visitor from abroad isn't expected to wear a kandūra; smart, modest clothes are fine. If you can't come after all, tell your host in good time.

title: It's not ḥarām, it's ʿēb
goal: At the door of Bū Rāshid's majlis, ask Sēf what's polite and what's rude
tip: ʿēb + a present verb means 'it's rude to': ʿēb tmidd ryūlak ṣōb in-nās 'it's rude to stretch your legs out towards people'. ʿēb is about manners: people will think you weren't brought up well. ḥarām is about religion: Islam forbids it. So a thing can be mub ḥarām, bas ʿēb.
grammar: ʿēb + verb 'it's rude to'; ʿēb (manners) vs ḥarām (religion)
dialogue: A
قبل لا ندش، النعال نخليها برا
gabil la ndishsh, in-niʿāl nkhallīha barra
Before we go in: we leave our shoes outside.
B
أكيد. وأسلم على منو أول؟
akīd. w asallim ʿala minu awwal?
Sure. And who do I greet first?
A
على عمي أول، هو الكبير
ʿala ʿammi awwal, huwa l-kbīr
My uncle first, he's the eldest.
B
زين. وفي شي عيب لازم أعرفه؟
zēn. w fī shay ʿēb lāzim aʿarfah?
OK. And is there anything rude I should know about?
A
هيه، عيب تمد ريولك صوب الناس
hē, ʿēb tmidd ryūlak ṣōb in-nās
Yes, it's rude to stretch your legs out towards people.
B
ليش؟ حرام؟
lēsh? ḥarām?
Why? Is it ḥarām?
A
مب حرام، بس عيب. الكبار ما يحبونه
mub ḥarām, bas ʿēb. il-kbār ma yḥibbūnah
It's not ḥarām, it's just bad manners. Older people don't like it.
B
فهمت. والقهوة آخذها باليمين
fhimt. w il-gahwa ākhidh-ha bil-yamīn
Got it. And I take the coffee with my right hand.
items: ʿēb ʿalēk! = shame on you! (to a man; to a woman: ʿēb ʿalēch); strong, said to children
allowed (by religion): ḥalāl (حلال); ḥarām ʿalēk = that's not fair
it's not forbidden, it's just rude
it's rude to stretch your legs out (to a man)
to a woman: ʿēb tmiddīn ryūlich (عيب تمدين ريولج)
a masculine thing: nkhallīh barra (نخليه برا)
who do I greet? who do I say hello to?
he's the eldest, he's the senior one
she's the eldest: hiya l-kbīra (هي الكبيرة)
culture: Majlis manners: shoes off at the door, greet the host and the eldest first, stand up when an older man comes in, and take and pass coffee with your right hand. Don't point the soles of your feet at anyone. ʿēb is the word parents use to teach all this, and ʿēb ʿalēk! 'shame on you!' is what children hear. Said to an adult, it's a strong rebuke.

title: Maghrib at the mosque
goal: Stop at a mosque with Sēf for the maghrib prayer: wudu, shoes, phone and what not to do
tip: Mosque rules use this block's forms: lāzim ma tmurr jiddām ḥad yṣalli 'you mustn't walk in front of anyone praying', ma yṣīr yrinn 'it mustn't ring'. New words: atwaẓẓa 'I do wudu', ʿala ṣ-ṣāmit 'on silent', ir-raff 'the shelf'.
grammar: recycle: lāzim ma, ma yṣīr (mosque rules)
dialogue: A
أذن المغرب. نصلي في هالمسجد؟
adhdhan il-maghrib. nṣalli fi hal-masjid?
That's the call for maghrib. Shall we pray at this mosque?
B
يلا. بس لازم أتوضى أول
yalla. bas lāzim atwaẓẓa awwal
Let's. But I need to do wudu first.
A
عادي، في مكان للوضوء ورا المسجد
ʿādi, fī makān lil-wuẓūʼ wara l-masjid
No problem, there's a place for wudu behind the mosque.
B
زين. ووين نخلي النعال؟
zēn. w wēn nkhalli n-niʿāl?
OK. And where do we leave our shoes?
A
في الرف يم الباب. وتلفونك خله على الصامت
fi r-raff yamm il-bāb. w tilifōnak khallah ʿala ṣ-ṣāmit
On the rack by the door. And put your phone on silent.
B
صح، ما يصير يرن والناس يصلون
ṣaḥḥ, ma yṣīr yrinn w in-nās yṣallūn
Right, it mustn't ring while people are praying.
A
وانتبه، لازم ما تمر قدام حد يصلي
w intibih, lāzim ma tmurr jiddām ḥad yṣalli
And careful: you mustn't walk in front of anyone who's praying.
B
إن شاء الله. يلا، الإمام بدا!
in shāʼ allāh. yalla, il-imām bada!
I won't. Come on, the imam's started!
items: UAE also: il-masīd (المسيد); this mosque: hal-masjid
I do wudu, I wash for prayer
he does wudu: yitwaẓẓa (يتوضى); you'll see written اتوضا
makān lil-wuẓūʼ = a place for wudu
tilifōnak khallah ʿala ṣ-ṣāmit = put your phone on silent (to a man); to a woman: tilifōnich khallīh ʿala ṣ-ṣāmit
you walk in front of, you pass in front of (to a man)
to a woman: tmurrīn jiddām (تمرين قدام)
culture: In a mosque, shoes go on the rack by the door, phones go on silent and voices stay low. Women pray in their own section, often with its own entrance. Most mosques have a washing area for wudu. If the prayer has started, join a row quietly, and never walk in front of someone who is praying. Afterwards people often say tagabbal allāh to each other.

title: It needs more time
goal: Tell Maryam what the project still needs before it goes to the manager
tip: yabā-lah + a noun means 'it needs': il-mashrūʿ yabā-lah wagt 'the project needs time'. The ending shows who or what needs it: yabā-lha for a feminine noun or plural things, yabā-li 'I need', yabā-lak 'you need'. ma yabā-lah means 'there's no need'.
dialogue: A
المشروع جاهز؟ المدير يبيه باكر
il-mashrūʿ jāhiz? il-mudīr yabīh bāchir
Is the project ready? The manager wants it tomorrow.
B
لا، للحين. يباله وقت شوي
la, lil-ḥīn. yabā-lah wagt shwayy
No, not yet. It needs a bit more time.
A
شو يباله بالضبط؟
shu yabā-lah biẓ-ẓabṭ?
What does it need, exactly?
B
العرض يباله صور، والأرقام يبالها مراجعة
il-ʿarẓ yabā-lah ṣuwar, w il-argām yabā-lha murājaʿa
The presentation needs pictures, and the figures need checking.
A
زين، الصور علي. وشو يبالك بعد؟
zēn, iṣ-ṣuwar ʿalay. w shu yabā-lak baʿad?
OK, leave the pictures to me. What else do you need?
B
يبالي يومين بس. نطرش للمدير إيميل؟
yabā-li yōmēn bas. nṭarrish lil-mudīr īmēl?
I just need two days. Shall we email the manager?
A
ما يباله، أنا بكلمه. انت خلص الأرقام
ma yabā-lah, ana bakallmah. inta khalliṣ il-argām
No need, I'll talk to him. You finish the figures.
B
ماشي. وطرشي لي الصور أول ما تخلصين
māshi. w ṭarrshī-li ṣ-ṣuwar awwal ma tkhallṣīn
OK. And send me the pictures as soon as you're done.
items: for a feminine noun or plural things: yabā-lha (يبالها); Kuwait: yabī-lah (يبيله)
it needs time, it'll take a while
ma yabā-lah tgūl-lah = no need to tell him
X ʿalay = leave X to me, I'll take care of X
to a woman: yabā-lich (يبالج); shu yabā-lak? = what do you need?
